title: Filter Even Numbers
description: Given an array of integers, return a new array containing only the even numbers, preserving order.
whatShouldHappen: Create an empty result array.
Loop through each element.
If the element is even (divisible by 2 with no remainder), push it into the result.
Return the result array.
patternExplanation: Build a new array by pushing only elements that satisfy a condition — the foundational pattern behind Array.prototype.filter.

title: Double Every Element
description: Given an array of numbers, return a new array where every element has been multiplied by 2.
whatShouldHappen: Create an empty result array.
Loop through each element.
Push the element multiplied by 2 into the result.
Return the result array.
patternExplanation: Apply a transformation to every element and collect the results — the foundational pattern behind Array.prototype.map.

title: Build Array from Permutation
description: Given a zero-based permutation nums (0-indexed), build and return an array ans of the same length where ans[i] = nums[nums[i]] for each 0 <= i < nums.length.
whatShouldHappen: Allocate a new array ans of length nums.length.
Iterate i from 0 up to nums.length - 1.
Assign ans[i] = nums[nums[i]].
Return the constructed array ans.
patternExplanation: Read values at index nums[i] and map them sequentially into the target buffer in O(n) time.

title: Concatenation of Array
description: Given an integer array nums of length n, return an array ans of length 2n where ans[i] == nums[i] and ans[i + n] == nums[i] for 0 <= i < n.
whatShouldHappen: Let n = nums.length.
Create an array ans of length 2 * n.
Iterate i from 0 to n - 1.
Populate ans[i] = nums[i] and ans[i + n] = nums[i].
Return the concatenated array ans.
patternExplanation: Writing to i and i + n in a single loop builds the doubled array with zero duplicate iteration overhead.

title: Pascal's Triangle
description: Given an integer numRows, return the first numRows of Pascal's triangle. In Pascal's triangle, each number is the sum of the two numbers directly above it.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize an empty triangle array.
For each row index i from 0 to numRows - 1, create a row array filled with 1s of size i + 1.
For column indices j from 1 to i - 1, set row[j] = triangle[i-1][j-1] + triangle[i-1][j].
Push row to triangle and return triangle when done.
patternExplanation: Build 2D triangular structure row by row, referencing the previous row's adjacent cells to calculate interior elements.

title: Generate 2D Grid Coordinates
description: Given rows and cols, construct a 2D matrix of dimensions rows x cols filled with row-major sequential integers starting from 1.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize grid = [] and counter = 1.
Iterate row from 0 to rows - 1.
In an inner loop, iterate col from 0 to cols - 1, pushing counter++ into the current row.
Push each completed row into grid and return grid.
patternExplanation: Nested loops cleanly populate multi-dimensional matrices in row-major order with sequential indexing.

title: Create Range with Step
description: Given integers start, end, and positive step, return an array of numbers starting at start and advancing by step while the value is strictly less than end. Use a for loop with compound addition (i += step).
whatShouldHappen: Initialize an empty result array.
Loop starting at i = start, continuing while i < end, incrementing by i += step.
Push each i into the result array.
Return result.
patternExplanation: Custom step increments in for loop headers (i += step) avoid unnecessary iterations and generate indexed sequences directly.

title: Running Product Array
description: Given an array of numbers nums, return a new array where the element at index i is the product of all elements from index 0 through i. For an empty array, return [].
whatShouldHappen: If nums is empty, return [].
Initialize result array and a running product accumulator to 1.
Iterate through nums, multiplying running product by nums[i].
Push running product into result.
Return result.
patternExplanation: Tracking a running prefix total/product and pushing intermediate values transforms a collection in O(n) single-pass time.

title: Alternate Interleave Arrays
description: Given two arrays arr1 and arr2, construct and return a new array alternating elements: take one from arr1, then one from arr2, until all elements from both arrays are included. If one array is longer, append its remaining elements at the end.
whatShouldHappen: Find max length between arr1 and arr2 using Math.max.
Loop index i from 0 up to max length.
If i < arr1.length, push arr1[i] to result.
If i < arr2.length, push arr2[i] to result.
Return result.
patternExplanation: Looping over the maximum length and guarding boundary checks for each array safely interleaves collections of unequal lengths.

title: Filter and Square Evens in Loop
description: Given an array of integers nums, build and return a new array containing the squares (num ** 2) of only the even numbers, maintaining their relative order. Do not use built-in .filter() or .map().
whatShouldHappen: Initialize an empty result array.
Iterate through nums with a loop.
Check if current element is even using num % 2 === 0.
If even, calculate square with num ** 2 and push to result.
Return result.
patternExplanation: Combining condition filtering (if num % 2 === 0) with mathematical transformation (num ** 2) within a single loop prevents multiple allocations.

title: Repeat Array Elements
description: Given an array arr and a non-negative integer times, construct and return a new array where every element of arr is repeated consecutive times times.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize an empty result array.
If times <= 0 or arr is empty, return [].
Loop through each item in arr.
For each item, run an inner loop from 0 to times, pushing item into result.
Return result.
patternExplanation: An outer loop over source items and an inner loop over repetition count constructs expanded sequence structures.
